questions.stem: ARCHIMEDES' PRINCIPLE states that the UPTHRUST on an object submerged in a fluid equals:

options.option_text: The weight of the fluid DISPLACED by the object

questions.explanation: Archimedes' Principle — upthrust (buoyant force) = weight of displaced fluid. If object's weight < weight displaced, it FLOATS. If equal, object is SUSPENDED. If weight > displacement, it SINKS. Explains ships staying afloat (steel, but overall density low).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: An object FLOATS on water if its density is:

options.option_text: Less than that of water (≤ 1 g/cc)

questions.explanation: Object floats if its AVERAGE density < density of fluid (water = 1 g/cc). Wood floats (~0.6 g/cc). Iron sinks (~7.8 g/cc) — but iron ships float because overall density (inc. hollow air-filled interior) < 1.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: It is EASIER to swim in SEA WATER than in RIVER water because:

options.option_text: Sea water has HIGHER DENSITY (from dissolved salts) → greater buoyant force

questions.explanation: Salt content makes sea water denser (~1.025 g/cc) vs fresh water (~1 g/cc). Greater fluid density → greater upthrust per unit volume submerged → object floats more easily. Dead Sea (~30% salinity, density ~1.24 g/cc) — people float effortlessly.

questions.stem: The SI unit of PRESSURE is:
questions.explanation: Pressure = Force / Area. SI unit: Pascal (Pa). 1 atm ≈ 101,325 Pa ≈ 1.01 bar. Tyre pressures often in 'bar' or 'psi'. Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude — hence planes pressurise cabins. 1 Pa = 1 N/m².
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: A HYDRAULIC LIFT works on the principle of:
questions.explanation: Pascal's law (1653) — small force on small piston creates same pressure everywhere in the fluid; a large piston with 100× area exerts 100× the force. Used in hydraulic lifts, brakes, jacks, presses. Amplifies force, not energy (same work done). pressure applied on a confined fluid is transmitted equally in all directions.

options.option_text: Why faster-flowing fluid has lower pressure

questions.explanation: Bernoulli's principle (1738) — in flowing fluid, speed and pressure trade off: higher speed → lower pressure. Applications: aeroplane lift (curved top of wing makes air flow faster → lower pressure above → lift), spinning ball curves in sports (Magnus effect), venturi flow meter. and how aeroplane wings generate lift.

questions.stem: DENSITY of pure water at 4°C is approximately:
questions.explanation: Water — maximum density at 4°C = 1 g/cc (or 1000 kg/m³). Water is UNUSUAL — it is LESS dense as ice (~0.92) than liquid → ice floats. This is because water molecules form a more open hexagonal lattice when freezing. Crucial for aquatic life (water bodies freeze from top).
